title: Exploratorium
description: Hundreds of hands-on science, art and perception exhibits on the waterfront at Pier 15, plus an outdoor bay observatory. Adults-only After Dark evenings run on select Thursday nights.

venue.name: Exploratorium, Pier 15
venue.address: Pier 15, The Embarcadero, San Francisco, CA

schedule: Open most days; check site for hours
tip: Grab a timed ticket online on weekends and pair it with a walk to the Ferry Building.

title: California Academy of Sciences
description: An aquarium, planetarium, natural history museum and four-story rainforest under one living roof in Golden Gate Park. Thursday NightLife evenings are 21+ with DJs and drinks among the exhibits.

venue.name: California Academy of Sciences
venue.address: 55 Music Concourse Dr, San Francisco, CA

tip: Head to the rainforest dome first — the line grows by midday.

title: de Young Museum & Hamon Observation Tower
description: Fine arts museum in Golden Gate Park known for American art, textiles and blockbuster exhibitions. The ninth-floor observation tower offers free 360° views over the park and city.

venue.name: de Young Museum
venue.address: 50 Hagiwara Tea Garden Dr, San Francisco, CA

tip: The free observation tower is one of the best rainy-day views in SF.

title: Legion of Honor
description: European art, Rodin sculptures and a neoclassical palace perched above Lands End with Golden Gate Bridge views.
tip: Combine with the Lands End Trail right outside for a perfect half-day.

title: SFMOMA
description: Seven floors of modern and contemporary art, from Warhol to Kahlo, plus a living wall and rooftop sculpture terraces in SoMa.

venue.name: San Francisco Museum of Modern Art

tip: The ground-floor galleries are free to wander — great for a quick art fix.

title: Ferry Building Marketplace & Ferry Plaza Farmers Market
description: The Bay's most famous food hall: oysters, bread, cheese, coffee and local makers inside a historic 1898 terminal. The CUESA farmers market sets up outside on Saturday mornings (plus Tuesdays and Thursdays).
schedule: Daily; farmers market Tue, Thu & Sat
tip: Saturday before 10am is the sweet spot for the market.

title: Lands End Trail & Sutro Baths
description: A rugged coastal trail with cypress groves, shipwreck views and the ruins of the Sutro Baths. One of the most dramatic free walks in the city.

venue.name: Lands End Lookout
venue.address: 680 Point Lobos Ave, San Francisco, CA

tip: Hunt for the hidden Lands End labyrinth on the cliffs.

title: Ocean Beach
description: Three-plus miles of wide, wild beach along the Outer Sunset and Richmond — made for long walks, kite flying and fiery sunsets (bundle up; the wind is real).
tip: Swimming is dangerous here — come for the views, not the waves.

title: Japanese Tea Garden
description: The oldest public Japanese garden in the U.S., with koi ponds, a drum bridge, pagoda and a tea house serving green tea and snacks.

venue.name: Japanese Tea Garden, Golden Gate Park
venue.address: 75 Hagiwara Tea Garden Dr, San Francisco, CA

tip: Go early on weekdays for quiet, misty mornings.

title: Conservatory of Flowers
description: A Victorian glass greenhouse in Golden Gate Park filled with orchids, carnivorous plants and a steamy lowland tropics room — a warm, green escape on a gray day.

venue.name: Conservatory of Flowers
venue.address: 100 John F Kennedy Dr, San Francisco, CA

tip: It's warm and humid inside — perfect when the fog is in.

title: Presidio Tunnel Tops
description: Fourteen acres of parkland built over the Presidio Parkway with picnic lawns, campfire circles, Golden Gate Bridge views and the nature-play Outpost for kids.
tip: Weekend food trucks and Crissy Field are steps away.

title: Musée Mécanique
description: A free-entry, coin-operated wonderland of antique arcade machines, fortune tellers and player pianos on the wharf. Bring quarters.

venue.name: Musée Mécanique, Pier 45
venue.address: Pier 45, Fisherman's Wharf, San Francisco, CA

tip: Laughing Sal is the star — and slightly terrifying.

title: Alcatraz Island
description: Tour the infamous federal penitentiary with the award-winning audio guide, then explore gardens and bird colonies on the Rock. Ferries leave from Pier 33.

venue.name: Alcatraz Landing, Pier 33
venue.address: Pier 33, The Embarcadero, San Francisco, CA

tip: Night tours sell out weeks ahead and are the most atmospheric.

title: Coit Tower & Telegraph Hill
description: Climb to Coit Tower for New Deal-era murals and panoramic views, then take the Filbert Steps down through hidden gardens (listen for the wild parrots).

venue.name: Coit Tower
venue.address: 1 Telegraph Hill Blvd, San Francisco, CA

tip: Walk up via the Greenwich or Filbert Steps instead of driving.

title: Mission Dolores Park
description: SF's sunniest social scene: picnic lawns, skyline views, a big playground and peak people-watching — usually warm when the west side is fogged in.

venue.name: Mission Dolores Park
venue.address: Dolores St & 19th St, San Francisco, CA

tip: Grab burritos or Bi-Rite ice cream on the way.

title: Alamo Square & the Painted Ladies
description: Picnic on the hill facing the famous row of Victorian houses with the downtown skyline behind — a quintessential SF postcard moment.

venue.name: Alamo Square Park
venue.address: Steiner St & Hayes St, San Francisco, CA

tip: Golden hour makes the best photos.

title: Twin Peaks Summit
description: Two windswept hilltops near the geographic center of SF with sweeping views of downtown, the bay and both bridges.

venue.name: Twin Peaks
venue.address: 501 Twin Peaks Blvd, San Francisco, CA

tip: Check for fog first — on a clear night the city lights are unreal.

title: Ride a Cable Car
description: Hop on the Powell–Hyde line for clanging bells, steep hills and bay views on the way to Ghirardelli Square. A rolling National Historic Landmark.

venue.name: Powell & Market Cable Car Turnaround
venue.address: Powell St & Market St, San Francisco, CA

tip: Board at the California St line for shorter lines.

title: Chinatown Walk from the Dragon Gate
description: Wander the oldest Chinatown in North America: dim sum, tea shops, herbal pharmacies, temples and alleyway murals along Grant Ave and Stockton St.

venue.name: Dragon Gate
venue.address: Grant Ave & Bush St, San Francisco, CA

tip: Watch fortune cookies being folded at the Golden Gate Fortune Cookie Factory on Ross Alley.

title: Castro Theatre
description: The landmark 1922 movie palace, restored and reopened, now hosting film series, concerts and comedy beneath its grand ceiling.
tip: Check the calendar for sing-alongs and classic film nights.

title: Roxie Theater
description: One of the oldest continuously operating cinemas in the country, screening indie, documentary and cult films in the Mission.
tip: Pair a late show with tacos on Valencia.

title: The Fillmore
description: The legendary rock hall where the '60s psychedelic scene was born. Still one of the best rooms in the country to catch a touring act — grab a free poster on sold-out nights.
tip: Don't skip the apple bucket by the door.

title: San Francisco Symphony at Davies Symphony Hall
description: World-class orchestra performances, film-with-live-orchestra nights and holiday concerts at Davies Symphony Hall in Civic Center.

venue.name: Davies Symphony Hall
venue.address: 201 Van Ness Ave, San Francisco, CA

tip: Look for rush and under-40 ticket deals.

title: Punch Line Comedy Club
description: A cozy, long-running Financial District club where big names test new material and rising comics cut their teeth.
tip: Weeknight showcases are cheap and often have surprise headliners.

title: Smuggler's Cove
description: A three-level, shipwreck-themed tiki bar with one of the deepest rum collections anywhere. Dangerous in the best way.
tip: Arrive right at opening to skip the line.

title: Bourbon & Branch
description: A Prohibition-style speakeasy behind an unmarked door in the Tenderloin — you'll need the password (and ideally a reservation).
tip: Book the library room for a date night.

title: The Midway
description: A Dogpatch creative complex with multiple rooms for dance parties, immersive art, live shows and late-night DJ sets.
tip: Check the calendar — themed parties sell out.

title: Golden State Warriors at Chase Center
description: Catch the Warriors (and the WNBA's Valkyries) at Chase Center in Mission Bay, plus big concerts and the surrounding Thrive City plaza.
tip: Thrive City hosts free outdoor watch parties on some game days.

title: San Francisco Giants at Oracle Park
description: Baseball with the best view in the majors: garlic fries, kayakers in McCovey Cove and the bay glittering past right field.

venue.name: Oracle Park
venue.address: 24 Willie Mays Plaza, San Francisco, CA

tip: Bring a jacket — evening games get cold fast.

title: Japantown & Japan Center Malls
description: Ramen, mochi, Japanese bookstores, photo booths and Peace Pagoda in one of only three remaining Japantowns in the U.S.
tip: The indoor malls make it a great rainy-day food crawl.

title: Balmy Alley Murals
description: A block-long outdoor gallery of vivid murals in the Mission, many tied to Central American history and community struggles.

venue.name: Balmy Alley
venue.address: Balmy St & 24th St, San Francisco, CA

tip: Precita Eyes offers guided mural walks on weekends.

title: Pier 39 Sea Lions
description: Hundreds of barking California sea lions lounging on the K-Dock floats — free, loud and guaranteed to delight kids.

venue.name: Pier 39
venue.address: Beach St & The Embarcadero, San Francisco, CA

tip: Numbers peak in fall and winter.

title: Aquarium of the Bay
description: Walk through clear tunnels as sharks, rays and local fish glide overhead — a compact aquarium focused on San Francisco Bay wildlife.
tip: Pair with the sea lions next door.

title: Children's Creativity Museum
description: Hands-on studios for kids to make claymation films, music videos and inventions, next to the historic carousel in Yerba Buena Gardens.
tip: Ride the 1906 Looff carousel out front.

title: San Francisco Zoo & Gardens
description: Lemurs, grizzlies, penguins and a lovingly restored carousel and little puffer steam train near Ocean Beach.

venue.name: San Francisco Zoo
venue.address: Sloat Blvd & Great Hwy, San Francisco, CA

tip: It stays cool here even on hot days thanks to the ocean breeze.

title: Mission Cliffs Climbing Gym
description: A huge indoor climbing gym with ropes, bouldering, yoga and fitness — a great rainy-day workout or first-climb date.
tip: Intro classes include gear and belay basics.

title: Kabuki Springs & Spa
description: Japanese-style communal baths with hot and cold plunges, steam and sauna in Japantown — the ultimate cozy reset on a drizzly day.
schedule: Daily; check co-ed and gender days
tip: Reserve bath entry ahead on weekends.

title: Yerba Buena Gardens
description: A downtown oasis of lawns, fountains and public art (including the MLK Jr. memorial waterfall), hosting free outdoor performances in warmer months.
tip: The rooftop playground and ice rink are on the Howard St side.

title: Baker Beach
description: A mile of sand facing the Golden Gate Bridge with wildflower bluffs and the Batteries to Bluffs trail above.
tip: The north end is clothing-optional — FYI for families.

title: Grace Cathedral
description: A Gothic cathedral atop Nob Hill with stained glass, Keith Haring's altarpiece and indoor and outdoor labyrinths open to all.
tip: Walk the outdoor terrazzo labyrinth at sunset.

title: City Lights Booksellers
description: The legendary Beat Generation bookstore and publisher in North Beach — browse poetry upstairs, then grab espresso next door.
tip: Vesuvio Cafe across Jack Kerouac Alley is the classic follow-up.

title: The Walt Disney Family Museum
description: An immersive museum of Walt Disney's life and the art of animation, inside historic barracks in the Presidio.
tip: Allow two hours — the galleries are deeper than you'd expect.

title: San Francisco Public Library – Main Library
description: A free, five-story civic hub with storytimes, a huge kids' center, teen lab, exhibits and author talks.
tip: Check the events calendar for free museum passes and workshops.

title: Golden Gate Bridge Walk
description: Walk or bike across the 1.7-mile span for jaw-dropping views of the city, Alcatraz and the Marin Headlands.

venue.name: Golden Gate Bridge Welcome Center
venue.address: Golden Gate Bridge Plaza, San Francisco, CA

tip: Bikers use the west sidewalk on weekends — check before you go.

title: Lake Merritt Loop
description: A 3.4-mile loop around Oakland's tidal lake with picnics, pedal boats, gardens and some of the best people-watching in the East Bay.
tip: Rent a gondola or pedal boat at the Lake Merritt Boating Center.

title: Oakland Museum of California
description: Art, history and natural sciences of California under one roof, with terraced rooftop gardens and lively community celebrations.
tip: Its Día de los Muertos exhibit each fall is a Bay Area tradition.

title: Chabot Space & Science Center
description: Hilltop planetarium, hands-on space exhibits and giant historic telescopes in the Oakland hills, with public telescope viewing on select evenings.
tip: Clear nights + telescopes = an epic date or family night.

title: Children's Fairyland
description: A storybook theme park on Lake Merritt for little kids, with puppet shows, gentle rides and whimsical sets (said to have inspired Disneyland).
tip: Adults need a child with them to enter.

title: Oakland Zoo
description: Animals in spacious habitats, a hilltop gondola with bay views and the California Trail exhibit of native wildlife.
tip: The gondola ride is worth it on a clear day.

title: Redwood Regional Park
description: Shady second-growth redwood trails just minutes from downtown Oakland — the Stream Trail stays cool even on the hottest days.
tip: Start at Skyline Gate for an easier, mostly-downhill loop.

title: Tilden Regional Park
description: Berkeley's backyard wilderness: a Little Farm, steam trains, a vintage carousel, botanic garden and Lake Anza for summer swims.
tip: Bring lettuce or celery for the Little Farm animals.

title: Lawrence Hall of Science
description: UC Berkeley's hands-on science center with interactive exhibits, a planetarium and a hilltop plaza with sweeping bay views.
tip: The view from the outdoor plaza alone is worth the drive.

title: UC Botanical Garden at Berkeley
description: Thirty-four acres of plants from around the world in Strawberry Canyon, from cactus gardens to a redwood grove.
tip: Check for free admission days.

title: Fox Theater Oakland
description: A dazzling 1928 movie palace turned concert hall in Uptown Oakland, hosting top touring bands and comedians.
tip: Uptown's bars and restaurants make easy pre-show stops.

title: Paramount Theatre Oakland
description: An Art Deco masterpiece hosting the Oakland Symphony, concerts, comedy and classic-movie nights with an organ overture.
tip: Join a docent-led building tour to see the Deco details up close.

title: Yoshi's Oakland
description: A storied jazz club and Japanese restaurant at Jack London Square with intimate sets from jazz, soul, R&B and funk greats.
tip: Dinner reservations get you better seats.

title: Freight & Salvage
description: Berkeley's nonprofit home for folk, bluegrass, blues and world music in a warm, all-ages listening room.
tip: Steps from Downtown Berkeley BART.

title: Berkeley Repertory Theatre
description: Tony Award-winning regional theater premiering bold new plays and musicals, many of which head to Broadway.
tip: Under-30 discounts are generous.

title: USS Hornet Sea, Air & Space Museum
description: Explore a WWII aircraft carrier that recovered the Apollo 11 astronauts — flight deck, hangar bays and vintage aircraft.
tip: Kids love the flight simulators.

title: Crown Memorial State Beach
description: Alameda's calm, shallow bay beach — warm-water wading, sandcastles and bike paths, with the Crab Cove visitor center nearby.
tip: Low tide at Crab Cove reveals tide-pool critters.

title: Mount Diablo State Park
description: Climb (or drive) to a 3,849-ft summit with one of the widest views in North America. The sunny-side escape when the coast is fogged in.
tip: Avoid midday hikes in summer — it gets hot.

title: Livermore Valley Wine Country
description: One of California's oldest wine regions, with 50+ relaxed, uncrowded tasting rooms just over the hills from the East Bay.
tip: Way less crowded than Napa — and often sunnier.

title: Ardenwood Historic Farm
description: A working 1890s farm in Fremont with farm animals, a horse-drawn train, Victorian house tours and seasonal harvest events.
tip: Fall brings a pumpkin patch and corn harvest.

title: Pillar Point Harbor & Half Moon Bay
description: Watch fishing boats unload, eat fresh fish and chips, walk the harbor bluffs and peek at Mavericks surf break on the San Mateo coast.

venue.name: Pillar Point Harbor
venue.address: 1 Johnson Pier, Half Moon Bay, CA

tip: Buy crab right off the boats in season.

title: Fitzgerald Marine Reserve Tide Pools
description: Some of the richest tide pools in California: sea stars, anemones, crabs and harbor seals at low tide in Moss Beach.
tip: Check a tide chart — aim for a minus tide.

title: CuriOdyssey
description: A small, hands-on science museum and wildlife center at Coyote Point with rescued animals and bay views.

venue.name: CuriOdyssey at Coyote Point
venue.address: 1651 Coyote Point Dr, San Mateo, CA

tip: Combine with the Coyote Point playground next door.

title: Filoli Historic House & Garden
description: A 1917 Georgian-style estate with 16 acres of formal gardens in Woodside — spectacular in tulip season and during the holidays.
tip: The holiday light displays are magical.

title: Cantor Arts Center at Stanford
description: A free museum with a 38,000-piece collection spanning 5,000 years, plus the Rodin Sculpture Garden outside.
tip: Don't miss the Anderson Collection next door, also free.

title: Hiller Aviation Museum
description: A century of flight at the San Carlos airport — vintage planes, a 747 cockpit and flight simulators.
tip: Check for special 'Open Cockpit' days.

title: Mori Point
description: A short, dramatic coastal trail in Pacifica with wildflowers, endangered frog ponds and big ocean views.
tip: Pair it with a walk on Pacifica Pier or a stop at Linda Mar Beach.

title: Winchester Mystery House
description: Sarah Winchester's sprawling, eccentric mansion with stairs to nowhere and doors that open onto walls — extra spooky in October.

venue.name: Winchester Mystery House
venue.address: 525 S Winchester Blvd, San Jose, CA

tip: Flashlight tours run on select nights.

title: The Tech Interactive
description: A hands-on science and technology center in downtown San Jose: design a robot, explore bioengineering and catch an IMAX dome film.

venue.name: The Tech Interactive
venue.address: 201 S Market St, San Jose, CA

tip: Great air-conditioned escape on a hot South Bay day.

title: Computer History Museum
description: The world's leading museum of computing history, from ancient calculators to the first Google server rack, in Mountain View.

venue.name: Computer History Museum
venue.address: 1401 N Shoreline Blvd, Mountain View, CA

tip: Catch the working Babbage Difference Engine demo if it's running.

title: Children's Discovery Museum of San Jose
description: A big purple museum packed with water play, a mammoth exhibit and hands-on zones for toddlers through tweens.
tip: Bring a change of clothes for the water exhibit.

title: San Pedro Square Market
description: An indoor-outdoor food hall in downtown San Jose with dozens of vendors, beer, live music and game-day crowds.

venue.name: San Pedro Square Market
venue.address: 87 N San Pedro St, San Jose, CA

tip: Busy before Sharks games at SAP Center.

title: Santana Row
description: A European-style outdoor shopping and dining district with patios, fire pits, a cinema and seasonal ice skating.
tip: Evenings are lively — great for a dinner date.

title: Shoreline Lake & Park
description: Rent sailboats, kayaks or paddleboards on a breezy saltwater lake in Mountain View, with bayside trails and birding.

venue.name: Shoreline Lake
venue.address: 3160 N Shoreline Blvd, Mountain View, CA

tip: Afternoon winds are great for sailing lessons.

title: Japanese Friendship Garden San Jose
description: A peaceful, free Japanese-style garden in Kelley Park with koi ponds, bridges and waterfalls.
tip: History Park is right next door.

title: Hakone Estate & Gardens
description: One of the oldest Japanese gardens in the Western Hemisphere, tucked into the Saratoga hills with tea ceremonies and moon viewing events.
tip: Pair with lunch in Saratoga Village.

title: California's Great America
description: Roller coasters, a water park in summer and spooky Halloween Haunt nights in the fall, in Santa Clara.

venue.name: California's Great America
venue.address: 4701 Great America Pkwy, Santa Clara, CA

tip: Weekday visits mean much shorter lines.

title: Rancho San Antonio Preserve
description: Miles of oak-studded foothill trails plus Deer Hollow Farm, beloved by South Bay hikers and kids alike.
tip: Lots fill early on weekends — arrive before 9am.

title: San Francisco 49ers at Levi's Stadium
description: NFL game days, mega-concerts and big events at Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara.

venue.name: Levi's Stadium
venue.address: 4900 Marie P DeBartolo Way, Santa Clara, CA

tip: Take VTA light rail or Caltrain + shuttle to skip parking.

title: San Jose Sharks at SAP Center
description: NHL hockey in 'The Shark Tank,' one of the loudest arenas in the league, plus concerts and family shows.

venue.name: SAP Center
venue.address: 525 W Santa Clara St, San Jose, CA

tip: Diridon Caltrain station is across the street.

title: Muir Woods National Monument
description: Walk among towering old-growth coast redwoods in a cool, hushed canyon just north of the Golden Gate. Parking or shuttle reservations required.

venue.name: Muir Woods
venue.address: 1 Muir Woods Rd, Mill Valley, CA

tip: Reserve parking ahead — you can't just show up.

title: Sausalito Waterfront
description: Stroll Bridgeway's galleries and cafés, gaze back at the SF skyline and peek at the colorful houseboat community. Arrive by ferry for the full experience.
tip: Take the Golden Gate Ferry from the Ferry Building.

title: Point Reyes National Seashore
description: Wild beaches, elk herds, a cliffside lighthouse and seasonal whale watching across 70,000+ acres on the Marin coast.

venue.name: Point Reyes National Seashore
venue.address: 1 Bear Valley Rd, Point Reyes Station, CA

tip: Grab picnic supplies in Point Reyes Station first.

title: Stinson Beach
description: A long, sandy Marin beach reached by a twisty coastal drive — the classic Bay Area summer beach day.
tip: Go early on hot weekends — Hwy 1 traffic backs up.

title: Mount Tamalpais State Park
description: Hike to East Peak for sunrise or sunset views over the whole Bay, or catch a summer show at the stone Mountain Theater.
tip: Above-the-fog sunsets here are unforgettable.

title: Bay Area Discovery Museum
description: A sprawling children's museum at the foot of the Golden Gate Bridge with a tot spot, lookout cove and art studios for kids under 10.
tip: Pack a picnic for the bridge-view lawn.

title: Marin Country Mart
description: A breezy open-air market of shops, restaurants and a weekly farmers market at the Larkspur ferry terminal.
tip: Take the ferry from SF and walk right in.

title: Sonoma Plaza
description: California's largest town plaza, ringed by tasting rooms, historic adobes, cafés and the Sonoma Mission — wine-country charm on foot.
tip: Tuesday evening farmers markets run in summer.

title: Napa Valley Wine Train
description: Gourmet dining aboard restored vintage rail cars on a scenic ride through Napa Valley vineyards.
tip: Book a window table for the best vineyard views.

title: Oxbow Public Market
description: A Napa food hall with oysters, tacos, coffee, spices and wine bars along the Napa River — an easy rainy-day wine-country stop.
tip: Hog Island oysters by the river is the move.

title: Charles M. Schulz Museum
description: A cheerful museum devoted to Peanuts creator Charles Schulz, with original strips, a Snoopy labyrinth and the ice arena next door.
tip: Skate at Snoopy's Home Ice across the street.

title: Six Flags Discovery Kingdom
description: A combined theme park and animal park in Vallejo with coasters, marine shows and seasonal Fright Fest.
tip: Take the SF Bay Ferry to Vallejo for a car-free trip.

title: Angel Island State Park
description: Ferry to the largest island in the bay for hiking, biking, picnics with 360° views and the moving Immigration Station museum.
tip: Bikes are allowed on the ferry — ride the 5-mile perimeter road.
